proposed_from.topic: A query-local beta-min phase boundary for finite-sample interventional causal representation learning. Fix Acarturk et al.'s deterministic population recovery program with a public smallest-label tie rule. For public g0,h0>0, let P_A(g0,h0) contain models whose every positive eigenvalue and nonzero projector comparison on that population transcript is at least g0 and h0, respectively; this is a model promise, never inferred from post-hoc empirical gaps. In the linear Gaussian variance-reset subclass with publicly conditioned observed covariances, construct an honest sequential certificate that returns the exact latent transitive closure and an approximate parent-supported encoder or abstains, with probability at least 1-alpha and polynomial sample dependence on n,kappa,g0^{-1},h0^{-1},log(1/alpha), but no unqueried subset margin. Prove that without a restriction excluding graph-changing weak alternatives, every uniformly alpha-valid randomized sequential procedure returns the correct singleton empty graph at the specified bounded-kernel logistic null with probability at most alpha. Finally, prove that for every n>=4 an explicit uniformly conditioned Gaussian bipartite family has reached gaps at least 1/40 and graph comparisons zero or one across n^2+2n-2 matrix occurrences, while the published all-subset margin is at most 2^(-2n-1) through the unqueried subset {3,4}. Use actual projector geometry, not the source's false printed angular expression. Consumer: add declared-gap certification, abstention/set output, and encoder error bars to the official finite-sample-linear-crl implementation. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fresh presolve derived ||Rhat_m-R_m||<=40*kappa^4*a from covariance error a, exact rank/projector intervals, transcript induction, and encoder-range error at most 4*sqrt(n)*e/g0. It proved the all-n Gaussian separation algebraically and independently checked exact transcripts, the 1/40 PSD inequality, and logistic forbidden-band exclusion at n=4,8,12,16. It also replaced a compressed source-membership argument by an explicit Legendre differential-operator construction and checked the weak-edge finite-prefix limit. Destructive checks covered path circularity, official exact-real ties, intervention legality, covariance conditioning, false angular and subset-pseudoinverse identities, repeated encoder eigenvalues, and accessible current literature; no collision survived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove that rational covariance, eigenspace, and projector-norm enclosures implement every decision with polynomial bit precision below a fixed fraction of the public tolerance. EARLY KILL TEST: run the certificate at the logistic null with positive-epsilon alternatives; any finite singleton claim without the public forbidden band contradicts the no-return theorem, while under g0 every sufficiently weak alternative must be excluded by a reached eigenvalue in (0,g0). seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 4--5, Algorithms 1--3, equation (22), Lemmas 13--19, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Replace the all-subset spectral margin in the deterministic Acartürk--Varıcı recovery proof by public gaps only on the matrices reached by a fixed smallest-label population transcript, and combine exact graph return with an encoder-range error bar or abstention.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: On the declared reached-gap class, an anytime-valid covariance certificate returns the exact latent transitive closure and a parent-supported encoder within a public error tolerance, with polynomial sample size and no unqueried-subset margin; without separation, honest singleton output is impossible at a regular null.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Lemma 13's uniform rank preservation over every subset by induction on the certified public transcript, propagating covariance, inverse, eigenspace, and projector-product intervals only after earlier decisions are certified.
seed_details.destination_search: A targeted search for interventional causal representation learning with confidence sequences, transcript-local eigengaps, and sequential abstention found Acartürk et al. (2024), Howard et al. (2021), and Lee et al. (2026), but no paper containing this target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Acartürk et al. because their primitive matrix event already holds for every subset and one can merely union-bound the executed queries.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability event is not the advance: the source theorem divides by the minimum positive eigenvalue over all subsets, while transcript induction permits models with exponentially small unqueried eigenvalues; Theorem 3 supplies such models for every dimension.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Summary, Introduction, Section 5, Theorem 1 and its nearby-alternative argument, and Section 10 discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Lift the pointwise-versus-uniform impossibility from observed-variable causal discovery to randomized sequential interventional CRL with adaptive environment selection and abstention.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: At an explicit bounded-kernel logistic empty-graph law, every uniformly \(\alpha\)-valid sequential rule has probability at most \(\alpha\) of any finite correct singleton return whenever graph-changing alternatives converge in every finite-prefix total variation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fixed-sample indistinguishability by an increasing sequence of finite-return events, expose all environment streams in advance, and pass from finite-prefix total variation to arbitrary randomized stopping by continuity from below.
seed_details.destination_search: Robins et al. (2003), Zhang and Spirtes (2003), Uhler et al. (2013), Kang and Hajek (2021), and Wang et al. (2026) settle nearby observed-graph, beta-min, binary-testing, and set-output questions; none treats latent interventional mixtures with randomized stopping.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Robins et al. because any graph-changing weak alternative rules out uniform consistency.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their experiment is observational and fixed-sample; admissible latent interventions, a common bounded score kernel, adaptive environment allocation, randomization, and the sharp null return bound all require a new explicit experiment and finite-prefix argument.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Algorithm 1, Algorithm 2, equation (22), Lemma 13, the projector perturbation argument in Lemmas 18--19, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Determine whether the published all-subset eigenvalue minimum is intrinsic to the executed CRL algorithm or only to its proof.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For every \(n\ge4\), construct a uniformly conditioned Gaussian bipartite model with constant spectral and projector gaps at all \(n^2+2n-2\) matrix occurrences of the fixed transcript but an unqueried subset eigenvalue at most \(2^{-2n-1}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Enumerate the exact matrix-occurrence transcript under the public tie rule and analyze the true projector product; do not use the printed subset-pseudoinverse or angular identity.
seed_details.destination_search: Acartürk et al. (2024) and Lee et al. (2026) retain all-subset spectral control, while Squires et al. (2023) supplies legal linear-Gaussian intervention geometry; no all-dimension separation family was located.
seed_details.red_team: A single cancellation example only shows that a loose proof constant can be small and says nothing about the algorithm.
seed_details.rebuttal: The family is uniform in dimension, keeps observed covariance conditioning bounded, enumerates every occurrence of the official transcript, and proves constant reached gaps alongside exponential off-path cancellation.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorems 1.1--1.2 and 3.3, Corollaries 4.4--4.5 on gaps and spectral projectors, Section 4.5 on stable inversion, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Turn the exact-real CRL certificate into a Turing-model algorithm whose rational enclosures cannot reverse a rank, repeated-eigenspace, or projector-norm decision.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Compose outward-rounded covariance inversion, Hermitian eigenspace enclosures, and projector-product norm bounds with precision polynomial in input length, \(n\), and \(\log(1/\min\{g_0,h_0\})\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace every exact spectral predicate by a certified rational interval and budget forward error across inverses, repeated invariant subspaces, and products before invoking the statistical tolerance.
seed_details.destination_search: Sobczyk (2025) gives deterministic bit bounds for Hermitian eigenvalues, gaps, and projectors, and Dey et al. (2023) give symbolic--numeric bit-growth accounting; no composition theorem for an adaptive CRL transcript was found.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by treating Sobczyk's projector routine and stable inversion as black boxes.
seed_details.rebuttal: The unresolved content is the end-to-end forward-error and precision composition through data-dependent matrix sums and zero-versus-positive projector norms, including repeated eigenvalues and rational covariance enclosures.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Definitions 1.1--1.4, the three-node cancellation construction in Section 2, the bipartite bounds, and Discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Invert sequential rank and projector tests to return a confidence set of latent transitive closures and encoder range classes when the public gap promise is withheld.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Construct an anytime-valid set-valued CRL output whose singleton event coincides with certified separation and whose noncoverage probability is at most \(\alpha\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace ordering-by-ordering regression test inversion by inversion of matrix spectral predicates along a branching CRL transcript.
seed_details.destination_search: Wang et al. provide asymptotic confidence sets for observed causal orderings, but the search found no finite-sample latent-interventional analogue with encoder uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: This is only the generic advice to return a confidence set rather than a graph.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable version needs a nontrivial branching spectral inversion algorithm and encoder range set; that construction is less mature than the fixed-transcript certificate and was therefore ranked out.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Definition 1, Theorems 1--3, the matrix and covariance applications in Section 4.3, and concluding discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Build operator-norm covariance confidence sequences for all intervention environments and feed them through an adaptive CRL decision transcript.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Obtain optional-stopping-valid covariance, inverse, rank, and projector intervals with a polynomial stopping bound under declared reached gaps.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Map the matrix supermartingale boundary to simultaneous covariance balls, then prove deterministic perturbation closure under the transcript rather than treating each terminal statistic as fixed in advance.
seed_details.destination_search: Howard et al. cover covariance confidence sequences and Acartürk et al. cover CRL perturbations, but no composition was found; by itself the composition is methodologically thinner than the phase-boundary package.
seed_details.red_team: A stagewise union bound or off-the-shelf confidence sequence makes this routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Optional-stopping coverage is standard, but pathwise permission to invoke only reached gaps and preserve public tie decisions requires a separate induction; this survives only as a component of the selected seed.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Assumptions 1--2, partial-order RQ construction, Theorems 1--3, Algorithms 1--2, and Discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Seek a finite-sample necessary-and-sufficient intervention-count boundary for exact linear-Gaussian causal disentanglement.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Characterize when one intervention per latent node remains sufficient and worst-case necessary after accounting for spectral separation and abstention.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Quantitize the partial-order RQ uniqueness argument and construct contiguous fewer-environment alternatives.
seed_details.destination_search: Squires et al. already prove population sufficiency and worst-case necessity, while Lee et al. (2026) match a logarithmic environment lower bound in another multi-node model; the finite-sample delta risks becoming a routine beta-min overlay.
seed_details.red_team: This is the published population intervention-count theorem plus standard concentration.
seed_details.rebuttal: A sharp finite-sample necessity could differ, but no nonroutine frontier beyond the selected transcript boundary was identified, so the seed was ranked out.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 3--4, Lemmas 3.1 and 4.2--4.4, Theorems 4.5--4.7, and Discussion.
seed_details.opportunity: Localize projection-based eigen-counting for unknown multi-node environments to subsets actually requested by the target-reconstruction algorithm.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Replace uniform control over all intervention-index subsets by a certified query family and quantify the resulting graph and decoder rates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Lemma 4.3's maximum over every nonempty subset by a path-conditional perturbation bound for the subset-intersection reconstruction routine.
seed_details.destination_search: Lee et al. provide the nearest target--method pair, but their different multi-node model and subset-reconstruction algorithm make a strict improvement difficult without rebuilding their combinatorial identification layer.
seed_details.red_team: The algorithm may genuinely need all subset intersections, so localization could be vacuous.
seed_details.rebuttal: The paper states only \(O(d)\) values are needed, suggesting a narrower query family, but the exact executed family was not sufficiently explicit to outrank the Acartürk transcript.
